note_sections.t: Specialist reassessment is requested due to a previous prostate cancer diagnosis coupled with a recent PSA increase to 6.9 ng/mL.

A 67-year-old retired warehouse worker initiated evaluation for prostate anomalies in 2024 after an initial PSA spike. Currently married yet residing independently, he relies on his adult son for emergency contact and his daughter for managing correspondence. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, notably nocturia and a diminished stream, yield an IPSS score of 17. Daily habits encompass a 20-minute walking routine and moderate alcohol intake averaging 16 units weekly. Recent outpatient screenings for hearing and actinic keratosis remain stable. He explicitly denies unexplained weight loss, skeletal pain, or haematuria, maintaining full independence in daily activities. Status: Ex-smoker (10 pack-yr, quit 2023).

Per rectum: Nodus DRE identifies a discrete, firm mass situated in the right peripheral zone, aligning with a cT2 classification. The remainder of the gland demonstrates symmetrical enlargement without additional abnormalities. Systemic assessment shows normal cardiorespiratory parameters. The individual maintains a well-nourished appearance and demonstrates unassisted mobility.
